mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate relative to historical averages compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors seek yield in equities.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 6.0% for two consecutive months, it signals weakening labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending confidence, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 6.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and rise in unemployment rate indicates a monetary policy response to economic weakness, which typically triggers a short-term equity market sell-off as recession risks increase over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when the joint movement of FEDFUNDS and UNRATE occurs and S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, a decline in housing starts below 1.7 million units annually signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when HOUST falls below 1.7 million units during late-cycle expansions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production above 105.0 index level indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: A retail sales level below 600,000 million dollars signals weak consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as economic momentum fades.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS falls below 600000.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low inflation, a monthly decline in the consumer price index below 0.1% (annualized rate < 1.2%) signals deflationary risks that prompt central bank rate cuts, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL monthly change is below 0.001.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth and rise in unemployment rate indicates a deteriorating labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending weakens and corporate earnings face headwinds.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises simultaneously.
